emily: quick check: bringing up ranky-v2-3b-ptq on short-doc cohort. with embed-scale=0.6 and max-doc-tokens=256 we see an MRR drop vs the fp16 baseline. anyone seen this pattern?

raj: numbers?

emily: baseline (ranky-v2-3b-fp16, embed-scale=1.0, max-doc-tokens=1024) => MRR@10=0.342, NDCG@10=0.421
new run (ptq, scale=0.6, max-doc=256) => MRR@10=0.298, NDCG@10=0.406

marta: hmm that's sizable. is the candidate encoder l2-normalized after scaling?

emily: yes pipeline is: embed -> multiply(scale) -> L2 norm -> dot-product with query. suspect scaling compresses norm variance especially for short docs.

jin: could be kvpack/kv-cache or truncation side-effects too. can you repro offline with identical candidate sets but varying scale? also try disabling L2 norm.

emily: repro plan (quick):
```
# run eval across scale and truncation settings
python eval.py \
  --model ranky-v2-3b-ptq \
  --embed-scale {0.6,1.0} \
  --max-doc-tokens {256,1024} \
  --cohort shortdocs \
  --disable-l2 {false,true}
```
collect ndcg/mrr per-query and plot delta by doc-length bucket.

eval-bot: run queued: eval-1728801300 (shortdocs, scale=0.6)

marta: also check embedding quantization artifacts: compare int8 per-channel rescale vs legacy table-based rescale. tag runs with quant_table=legacy/perchannel.

raj: one-off thought: truncation chops different parts of the doc which for short docs might remove unique tokens; but less likely for very short docs. also check tokenizer parity between offline preproc and prod (casefold/punctuation).

emily: good catch. i'll run tokenizer parity check and a full holdout run. will also capture per-query token counts and top-1 changes.

jin: if this reproduces, we should consider a short-doc routing fallback: route short-doc traffic to fp16 variant until we patch scoring.

emily: agreed. tentative follow-ups:
- emily: repro + tokenizer parity (ETA ~2h)
- marta: quant table probes (ETA ~4h)
- jin: routing fallback prototype (ETA EOD)

emily: will upload CSV + plots here when done :eyes:
